parent_models.justification: Matrix factorization is the general field from which nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) originates. NMF is a specific type of matrix factorization, therefore matrix factorization serves as the parent model for NMF.

closest_parent_model.justification: Since matrix factorization is the direct and general method from which nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) is derived, it is considered the closest parent model.

closest_child_model.justification: By definition, a child model would be more specific within the given NMF scope, but since there are no child models in the list that specify any specialization of NMF, NMF itself stands as the most specific model in the context of the existing list.

sibling_models.justification: Hidden interaction tensor factorization is a method related to factorizing mathematical structures like NMF but involves tensor factorization instead; thus, it shares conceptual space at the level of matrix or tensor decomposition.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Hidden interaction tensor factorization is closely related due to its focus on factorization, similar to nonnegative matrix factorization, but with tensors instead of matrices, making it the closest sibling in the space of factorization methods.
